hints.title: Ranking Daily Amounts
hints.text: Partition transaction records by the day date and order each day transactions by amount descending.

hints.title: Handling Ties with Dense Ranking
hints.text: Use the dense_rank window function to assign rank 1 to all transactions tied for the maximum amount of that day.

hints.title: Filtering and Sorting Output
hints.text: Filter ranked records for rank 1 and sort transaction identifiers in ascending order.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH Ranked AS (
    SELECT
        transaction_id,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(day) ORDER BY amount DESC) AS rk
    FROM Transactions
)
SELECT transaction_id
FROM Ranked
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY transaction_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) window sort over daily partition buckets
complexity.space: O(N) working memory for window evaluation
complexity.notes: Window ranking partitioned by calendar day.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries scanning the daily max per row take quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window ranking processes all partitions in a single sorted pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that ties for the maximum amount must all be included using dense_rank.

WITH Ranked AS (
    SELECT
        transaction_id,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(day) ORDER BY amount DESC) AS rk
    FROM Transactions
)
SELECT transaction_id
FROM Ranked
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY transaction_id ASC;

WITH Ranked AS (
    SELECT
        transaction_id,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(day AS DATE) ORDER BY amount DESC) AS rk
    FROM Transactions
)
SELECT transaction_id
FROM Ranked
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY transaction_id ASC;
